subject: Governance & SLA alignment for renewal — QBR and capacity planning
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@saturnsys.com>, ops@saturnsys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Governance & SLA alignment for renewal — QBR and capacity planning

Hi Emma / Saturn ops team,

Thanks for the productive sync last week. As we move toward the renewal conversation for SS-7839, I'd like to kick off a short governance and capacity alignment thread so we can lock timelines and owners before the QBR. Attached is an initial renewal proposal and a capacity forecast (rough numbers) to prime the discussion.

High-level asks from Redwood:
- Confirm term preference (12 vs 24 months) and whether you want a stepped commit vs flat monthly.
- Validate SLO targets — currently proposing 99.95% monthly uptime for the Dedicated pool and 200ms p50 / 600ms p95 for typical gen requests.
- Indicate anticipated burst windows (dates or monthly % spikes) so we can plan reserved vs burst capacity.
- Provide primary legal/ procurement contact for contract cadence.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick intake QBR (30 min) to review proposal and surface blockers — please pick one of the slots in the attached ICS.
2) Redwood to share an updated commitment/ pricing matrix after we confirm term length and expected qtr-on-qtr growth.
3) Tech/ infra working sync (45 min) to go over capacity runbook, on-call escalation, and KV-cache warming for your high-throughput endpoints.

Notes on governance we want to confirm during QBR: escalation SLAs for incidents, audit-log retention for your compliance team, and a fallback policy (model variant/regional fallback) if Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Emma, is there anyone else on your side we should include? If ops@saturnsys is a distribution list, great — otherwise please loop in Lydia from procurement.

Thanks — I can own logistics.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attach: renewal-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal, 6 pages); capacity-forecast-q3-q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@saturnsys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@saturnsys.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Governance & SLA alignment for renewal — QBR and capacity planning

Hi Irene — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks.

On term: executive leadership prefers a 12-month with optional uplift at Q3 depending on usage — can you model a step-up at month 9?

On SLOs: the 99.95% uptime sounds reasonable, but we need a written definition (incidents that qualify, measurement window). Also want clarity on your planned regional fallback behavior — we cannot fail to EU during our morning-window (00:00-06:00 UTC) due to regulatory routing.

Burst windows: we expect predictable spikes during our billing run on the first 3 business days of each month and a larger annual spike in late November (Blackstone release).

I'll confirm Lydia's email and loop her in — for now ops@saturnsys will triage. Can we aim for the QBR week of Sep 28? We have constrained windows but can do Sep 29 at 10:00am PT if that works.

Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, Saturn Systems

Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Governance & SLA alignment for renewal — QBR and capacity planning

Thanks team — I'll draft the incident SLA language this afternoon. Quick notes I'll bring to the QBR:
- Proposed incident classification (P1/P2/P3) with response and remediation windows; include a blameless post-mortem cadence.
- Escalation contact matrix (on-call + pager rotation) and optional dedicated webhooks for Saturn's PagerDuty.
- A fallback policy: if Dedicated pool utilization > 85% for more than 2 hours, traffic will fail over to a cheaper model variant in a secondary region while we provision burst capacity. We'll document allowed variance and customer opt-outs.

Karthik — please surface the KV-cache warmup plan and an estimate of warmup token cost (ballpark).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
